why: offset everywhere incl. toc and CLI, validated, documented and tested
prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Added `heading_offset` (0–5, default 0, anything else raises `ValueError`) to `markdown.Markdown`/`markdown.markdown` and `--heading-offset N` to the command line; the full test suite passes (1150 tests, 112 skipped as before; no linter is installed here, so style was not machine-checked). The shift is done by a new built-in tree processor (`heading_offset`, priority 25), so it covers hash, underline, `md_in_html` and footnote headings and runs before `toc`, whose tokens and `toc_depth` see the shifted levels. Raw HTML headings without `markdown="1"` are left alone, since Markdown passes them through rather than producing them. `toc`'s `baselevel` stacks on top of the offset. Booleans, floats such as `1.0` and strings such as `'1'` are rejected as not whole numbers. On the command line a bad value exits with a usage error rather than a traceback. Tests, docs (library, CLI, toc, extension API) and an Unreleased changelog entry are included; nothing is committed.
